thread:
Alex: Heads up — seeing a 25-40ms per-token latency spike on /v1/generate for the 'dialogue' route starting ~10:20 UTC. Spike lines up with kernel fallback to generic GEMM on a subset of requests and a KV cache hitrate drop (94% -> 67%).

Alex: Log excerpt:```
[2026-03-18T10:20:12Z] request_id=rq_9f2a trace_id=tr_0a3b kernel=generic_gemm fwd_ms=18 per_token_ms=32 kv_hit=false
[2026-03-18T10:20:12Z] request_id=rq_9f2b trace_id=tr_0a3c kernel=quantized_fp16 fwd_ms=6 per_token_ms=8 kv_hit=true
[2026-03-18T10:20:13Z] request_id=rq_9f2c trace_id=tr_0a3d kernel=generic_gemm fwd_ms=21 per_token_ms=35 kv_hit=false
```

Priya: Thanks. Do we have full traces for those trace_ids? Any repro in perf-canary? I ran a quick profiler yesterday and saw kernel selection oscillating around seq_len ~512 boundary for mixed batches.

Alex: Put 3 trace ids above (tr_0a3b tr_0a3c tr_0a3d). I can reproduce locally with a small harness when I force mixed batch shapes. Repro script logs kernel_selector decisions and kv checks.

Sam: I can add a "jump-to-trace" action to the per-request table on the dashboard. Pattern we use: https://console.redwood/traces/{trace_id} . Suggest we inject trace_id into metric labels so the dashboard row links directly. Eg:```
metric('request_latency_ms', labels={ 'route':route, 'kernel_variant':kernel, 'trace_id':log.trace_id })
```

Marta: FWIW autoscaler pulsed at the same time and created mixed-batch composition. Batching heuristic picked a small batch path where quantized kernels aren't applicable for certain alignment/seq combos. That forces the runtime to choose the generic kernel. We should tag batch_shape and kernel_variant on the request timeseries.

Priya: Agreed — token-level breakdown widget + per-route KPI for "percent optimized-kernel" would make it obvious when this is happening. Also: can we emit a small gauge that flags kernel_fallback=true for the request? That would make alerting trivial.

Alex: Good idea. For observability: the immediate useful fields per request are: trace_id, route, kernel_variant, kv_hit, batch_shape, per_token_ms. If Sam can drop a temporary dashboard listing recent requests with those fields, we can triage faster.

infra-bot: deploy: hotfix/kernelfilter rolled to prod at 1765432275 by Dave (reason: temporary filter to prefer quantized kernels for seq_len<=512). :rocket:

Dave (infra): Rolled the hotfix. Observed a small improvement in kernel mix but KV hitrate still ~72% in the affected minute. Re-running microprofiler now to capture low-level kernel timings.

Sam: On it — creating a dashboard card now that lists the last 200 requests (trace_id, route, kernel_variant, kv_hit, batch_shape, per_token_ms) with a link action to traces. Will include a quick filter for route='dialogue'. ETA ~30m. @Marta for quick review once done. :eyes:

Marta: I'll watch the canary after the dashboard goes live. If autoscaler continues to create many small batches we should tweak burst policy and prefer coalescing for these routes.

Priya: Opening PERF-REG-452 ticket with repro script, profiler output, and sample trace ids. I'll paste the ticket link here when complete. Initial mitigation plan: 1) emit kernel_fallback gauge, 2) add dashboard row + trace jump, 3) test autoscaler burst adjustments in canary.

Alex: Thanks — once dashboard is up I'll attach the reproduction harness output. Short-term triage checklist for anyone jumping in: 
- Use dashboard filter route=dialogue
- Click trace for requests showing kernel_variant=generic_gemm
- Check kv_hit and batch_shape in the row
- Run local harness with the same batch_shape to repro

Priya: Ticket created: https://issues.redwood/PERF-REG-452 (contains repro script + raw profiler zips).

Sam: Dashboard card pushed to staging (card id=card_786). Linking to prod once reviewed. Added a quick alert rule: kernel_fallback_rate(route='dialogue') > 5% for 5m.

Alex: Nice. Once the trace links are wired we'll be able to correlate the per-token waterfall with kernel selection and KV misses quickly. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
